youtube_title: Notre Dame's Washington Hall: the legend of George Gipp's ghost
body: Students at Notre Dame say Washington Hall, the old campus theater, is haunted, and many say by George Gipp. In 1920 the football star became Notre Dame's first Walter Camp All-American, and on Dec. 14, 1920, he died after an illness reported as strep throat and pneumonia. He was 25. Legend says he got locked out after curfew and slept on the hall's steps, but there's no evidence of that. By 1921 students wrote of footsteps and a phantom horn, and years later a student said he saw Gipp's ghost ride a white horse up the steps. In 1928 Knute Rockne told his team Gipp's dying wish was to "win one for the Gipper" (no one can prove Gipp said it), and they beat Army 12-6. 🏈👻 Comment your town, and it could be next! #NotreDame #SouthBend #GeorgeGipp #Indiana #History #Haunted #LaPorteAfterDark

Gipp was Notre Dame's first Walter Camp All-American in 1920. On Dec. 14, 1920, he died after an illness reported as strep throat and pneumonia. He was 25.
Legend says he got locked out after curfew and slept on Washington Hall's steps. There's no evidence of that. By 1921 students wrote of footsteps and a phantom horn in the hall, and years later one said he saw Gipp's ghost ride a white horse up its steps.
